blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Chapter 17 (Alternating Current), arranged by the chapter's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each answer is a short model answer; small numericals show the working, and a comparison is answered as a table.

blocks.prompt: 1 What is meant by alternating current? Write the equation of an alternating voltage.
blocks.explanation: Alternating current is a sinusoidally varying current that can be represented by time dependent sine or cosine functions. The emf of an AC generator is V = Vₒ sin ωt, where Vₒ is the peak voltage and ω the angular frequency; similarly I = Iₒ sin ωt.

book_ref.quote: An alternating current AC means a sinusoidally varying current

blocks.prompt: 2 What two conditions must a periodically varying voltage satisfy to be called alternating?
blocks.explanation: (i) Every cycle has two exactly symmetrical half-cycles, one positive and one negative, so the polarity reverses after every half-cycle. (ii) The peak value on both sides stays constant in all cycles.

book_ref.quote: A periodically varying current or voltage is termed as alternating

blocks.prompt: 3 Define time period and frequency of an alternating quantity. How are they related?
blocks.explanation: Time period T is the time taken to complete one cycle (in seconds). Frequency f is the number of cycles in one second (in hertz, 1 Hz = 1 cycle per second). They are related by f = 1/T.

book_ref.quote: The time taken to complete one cycle of an alternating quantity is called its time period

blocks.prompt: 4 An alternating voltage completes one cycle in 0.02 s. Find its frequency and angular frequency.

book_ref.quote: Frequency (f): The number of cycles that occur in one second is called its frequency.

blocks.prompt: 5 Where does an alternating voltage change most rapidly and where most slowly?
blocks.explanation: It changes most rapidly at the zero (crossover) points and most slowly at its peaks, where it momentarily reaches its maximum value.

book_ref.quote: changes occur most rapidly at the zero (crossover) points and most slowly at its peak

blocks.prompt: 6 Why is AC preferred over DC for supplying electricity between cities?
blocks.explanation: AC can be transferred easily over long distances, even between two cities, without much energy loss, whereas DC cannot be transferred over a very long distance because it loses electric power.

book_ref.quote: DC cannot be transferred over a very long distance.

blocks.prompt: 7 Why is the average value of a sinusoidal AC over a full cycle zero? Over which part is the average value usually taken?
blocks.explanation: Over a full cycle (0 to 2π) the positive and negative half-cycles are mirror images and cancel out perfectly, so the average is zero. Hence the average value usually means the average over one half-cycle (0 to π).

book_ref.quote: This happens because the positive half-cycle and the negative half-cycle are mirror images of each other.

blocks.prompt: 8 The peak value of a full-wave rectified voltage is 50 V. Find its average value.

book_ref.quote: For a full-wave rectified sine wave, the average values of current and voltage are given by

blocks.prompt: 9 Define peak value and peak-to-peak value of an alternating voltage. How are they related for a sine wave?
blocks.explanation: Peak value Vₒ is the highest value the waveform reaches in one cycle (top of the positive or bottom of the negative half-cycle). Peak-to-peak value is the total distance from the positive peak to the negative peak. For a symmetrical sine wave Vp-p = 2Vₒ.

book_ref.quote: It is the highest value that an AC waveform reaches during one cycle.

blocks.prompt: 10 What is instantaneous value? Write the instantaneous voltage in terms of frequency.
blocks.explanation: The value of an AC quantity at any instant of time is its instantaneous value: V = Vₒ sin ωt. Since ω = 2π/T and f = 1/T, V = Vₒ sin (2πft).

book_ref.quote: The value of an AC quantity at any instant of time is known as instantaneous value.

blocks.prompt: 11 Why are rms values used to compare an alternating current with a direct current?
blocks.explanation: rms values are the direct current or voltage values that produce the same heating effect (power dissipation) as the alternating current or voltage, so they give the equivalent DC value of an AC: Iᵣₘₛ = 0.707 Iₒ, Vᵣₘₛ = 0.707 Vₒ.

book_ref.quote: The rms values represent the direct current, or voltage, values that will produce the same heating effect

blocks.prompt: 12 The rms value of a supply voltage is 120 V. Find its peak and peak-to-peak values.

book_ref.quote: So, rms current, Iᵣₘₛ is equal to 0.707 Iₒ

blocks.prompt: 13 Why do high voltage power lines crackle and hiss?
blocks.explanation: Because of corona discharge: the strong electric field ionises the air around the conductor when the voltage exceeds the breakdown strength of air. This discharge gives a glow, radio noise and a hissing or crackling sound.

book_ref.quote: the air surrounding the conductor becomes ionized due to a strong electric field

blocks.prompt: 14 How can you tell whether a current is alternating or direct?
blocks.explanation: Find the direction of the current and see whether it changes. If the current periodically reverses its direction it is alternating current; if it flows in a single direction it is direct current.

book_ref.quote: Determine whether the current's direction changes or stays the same.

blocks.prompt: 15 How can the presence of AC in a wire under a carpet be detected?
blocks.explanation: With a non-contact voltage detector (pen tester), which senses the electromagnetic field of the current and shows it by a light or sound, or with a multimeter on the AC voltage setting for a more precise measurement.

book_ref.quote: Non-contact detectors will sense the electromagnetic field generated by the current

blocks.text: 17.2 Relation Between Mean Power and Maximum Power for an Alternating Current

blocks.prompt: 16 Define instantaneous power and mean power in an AC circuit.
blocks.explanation: Instantaneous power is the power at any given moment t: P = VI, with V and I the instantaneous voltage and current. Mean power Pₘₑₐₙ is the average power over one complete cycle of the AC waveform; for a resistor Pₘₑₐₙ = Iᵣₘₛ²R.

book_ref.quote: The instantaneous power P in a circuit is the power at any given moment in time t.

blocks.prompt: 17 Why is the mean power in a resistive load only half of the maximum power?
blocks.explanation: Because the instantaneous power varies over the cycle: it reaches its maximum value only at certain points and spends significant time at zero or lower values, so its average is half the peak: Pₘₑₐₙ = Pₘₐₓ/2.

book_ref.quote: the mean power in a resistive load is half the maximum power

blocks.prompt: 18 An rms current of 3 A flows through a 40 Ω resistor. Find the mean power and the peak power.
blocks.explanation: Pₘₑₐₙ = Iᵣₘₛ²R = (3 A)² × 40 Ω = 360 W. Pₘₐₓ = 2Pₘₑₐₙ = 720 W.

book_ref.quote: Also we have expression for the mean power Pₘₑₐₙ represented by

blocks.prompt: 19 What is a resistive load?
blocks.explanation: A resistive load is one that does not store energy (as a capacitor or an inductor does) but simply dissipates the energy as heat.

book_ref.quote: A resistive load is one that does not store energy

blocks.prompt: 20 Define phase of an alternating quantity. Give the phases of the points at the start, the positive peak and the end of one cycle.
blocks.explanation: Phase is the angle θ (= ωt) which specifies the instantaneous value of an alternating voltage or current. At the start of a cycle the phase is 0, at the positive peak π/2 and at the end of the cycle 2π.

book_ref.quote: The angle θ which specifies the instantaneous value of the alternating voltage or current is called the phase.

blocks.prompt: 21 What is initial phase? What is meant by the current leading the voltage?
blocks.explanation: The phase angle at t = 0 is the initial phase. If V = Vₒ sin θ and I = Iₒ sin (θ + φ), at t = 0 V = 0 but I = Iₒ sin φ; the current reached zero earlier by φ, so the current leads the voltage by φ.

book_ref.quote: the value of the phase angle θ at t equals to zero is called the initial phase

blocks.prompt: 22 Differentiate between current leading and current lagging the voltage.
blocks.explanation: Leading: current reaches zero earlier than the voltage; lagging: it reaches zero later.

book_ref.quote: It means that the current I will reach its zero value later on by an angle φ than the voltage V.

rows: I = Iₒ sin (θ + φ), with V = Vₒ sin θ.
I = Iₒ sin (θ − φ), with V = Vₒ sin θ.
At t = 0, I = +Iₒ sin φ.
At t = 0, I = −Iₒ sin φ.
Current reaches its zero value earlier by φ.
Current reaches its zero value later by φ.

blocks.prompt: 23 State the conditions for representing an alternating quantity by a rotating vector.
blocks.explanation: The vector rotates anticlockwise and (i) its length on a scale represents the peak or rms value; (ii) it is horizontal at the instant when the quantity is zero and increasing positively; (iii) its angular frequency equals that of the alternating quantity.

book_ref.quote: An alternating quantity can be represented by an anticlockwise rotating vector

blocks.prompt: 24 Name the basic circuit elements of DC and AC circuits.
blocks.explanation: In a DC circuit the basic element is a resistor R, which controls current and voltage through Ohm's law V = IR. In an AC circuit the basic elements are resistor R, inductor L and capacitor C.

book_ref.quote: But the basic circuit elements in AC circuit are resistor R, inductor L and capacitor C.

blocks.prompt: 25 Show that voltage and current are in phase in a purely resistive AC circuit.
blocks.explanation: With V = Vₒ sin ωt, I = V/R = (Vₒ/R) sin ωt = Iₒ sin ωt. Both are sine functions of the same ωt, so they pass their maximum and minimum values at the same time: they are in phase.

book_ref.quote: both voltage and current pass their minimum and maximum values at the same time

blocks.prompt: 26 Why does the power dissipated in a resistor not depend on the direction of the current?
blocks.explanation: Because the power dissipation is proportional to the square of the current (P = I²R). The square is positive whether the current is positive or negative, so it makes no difference whether the current is direct or alternating.

book_ref.quote: The power dissipation is proportional to the square of the current

blocks.prompt: 27 A 1.2 kW heater works on a 240 V AC supply. Find the current taken and the resistance of the heater when hot.

book_ref.quote: A 1 kW heating element is connected to a 250 V AC supply voltage.

blocks.prompt: 28 Why are doorbells often operated on 12 V AC?
blocks.explanation: Low-voltage AC is safer to handle and reduces the risk of electrical shock.

book_ref.quote: 12 V A.C DOORBELL Low-voltage AC is safer to handle

blocks.prompt: 29 What is an inductor? How does it slow down current surges?
blocks.explanation: An inductor (coil or choke) is a passive two-terminal component with a large self-inductance and negligible resistance that stores energy in a magnetic field. It slows down surges by temporarily storing energy in its field and then releasing it back into the circuit.

book_ref.quote: The inductor is used to slow down current surges or spikes

blocks.prompt: 30 Define inductive reactance. On what factors does it depend?
blocks.explanation: Inductive reactance X_L is the opposition offered by an inductor to AC: X_L = Vᵣₘₛ/Iᵣₘₛ = ωL = 2πfL. It is directly proportional to the frequency f and the inductance L. Its unit is ohm.

book_ref.quote: The resistance offered by an inductor is called inductive reactance

blocks.prompt: 31 Why does an inductor allow DC but block AC?
blocks.explanation: X_L = 2πfL. For DC, f = 0, so X_L = 0 and the inductor offers no reactance. For AC of large frequency, X_L is large, so the inductor strongly opposes (blocks) the AC.

book_ref.quote: Thus, we conclude that an inductor allows DC but blocks the AC.

blocks.prompt: 32 Find the inductive reactance of a 50 mH coil at 1 kHz.

book_ref.quote: It shows that inductive reactance X_L is directly proportional to both

blocks.prompt: 33 Why is the average power dissipated in a pure inductor zero?
blocks.explanation: The voltage and current in a pure inductor differ in phase by 90°. The inductor stores energy in its magnetic field in one quarter-cycle and returns it to the source in the next, so the average power over a cycle is zero.

book_ref.quote: The average power dissipated in a pure inductor is zero.

blocks.prompt: 34 A coil of 0.3 H and negligible resistance carries an rms current of 10 mA at 200 Hz. Find the rms voltage across it.

book_ref.quote: Inductance of the coil L = 400 mH = 400 × 10⁻³ H

blocks.prompt: 35 What is a choke? Why is its inductance very high?
blocks.explanation: A choke is a coil of thick copper wire wound closely in a large number of turns over a soft iron laminated core. Its inductance L is very high because of the high permeability of the iron core.

book_ref.quote: It is a coil of thick copper wire wound closely in a large number of turns over a soft iron laminated core.

blocks.prompt: 36 Why is practically no power dissipated as heat in a choke coil?
blocks.explanation: The resistance of a choke is negligibly small while its reactance is large, so its power factor cos θ is almost zero and θ is nearly 90°. Since P = VI cos θ, practically no power is dissipated as heat.

book_ref.quote: So practically, no power is dissipated as heat by a choke coil.

blocks.prompt: 37 Give two uses of choke coils in electronic circuits.
blocks.explanation: (i) They filter out high frequency AC noise from electronic circuits, giving a cleaner DC output. (ii) In switch-mode power supplies they help to regulate voltage and filter out switching noise. They also stop unwanted RF signals leaking out of circuits.

book_ref.quote: Choke coils are used to filter out high frequency AC noise from electronic circuits

blocks.prompt: 38 What is the role of a choke in a fluorescent light?
blocks.explanation: The choke generates transient (sudden) voltages across the tube, which help the gas inside reach its breakdown voltage so the tube lights. Chokes also limit the rate of current change, protecting insulation from sudden surges.

book_ref.quote: Chokes in fluorescent lights generate transient voltages across the tube

blocks.prompt: 39 Why does a capacitor block DC while an inductor allows it?
blocks.explanation: For DC, f = 0. Then X_L = 2πfL = 0, so the inductor acts as a conductor; but X_C = 1/(2πfC) = 1/0 = ∞, so the capacitor blocks DC.

book_ref.quote: Why capacitor and inductor behaves differently for AC and DC?

blocks.prompt: 40 How does alternating current flow in a circuit containing a capacitor when no charge crosses its insulating medium?
blocks.explanation: As the applied voltage reverses, the capacitor is charged first in one direction and then in the other. Electrons therefore move to and fro around the circuit connecting the plates, which constitutes an alternating current.

book_ref.quote: But alternating current can pass through a capacitor.

blocks.prompt: 41 Define capacitive reactance and write its formula and unit.
blocks.explanation: Capacitive reactance X_C is the opposition offered by a capacitor to AC: X_C = Vᵣₘₛ/Iᵣₘₛ = 1/ωC = 1/(2πfC). Its unit is ohm.

book_ref.quote: Resistance offered by capacitor is known as capacitive reactance

blocks.prompt: 42 How does the current through a capacitor change with the frequency of the supply?
blocks.explanation: X_C = 1/(2πfC). At low frequency X_C is large and the current is small; at high frequency X_C is small and the current through the same capacitor is large.

book_ref.quote: for low frequencies, capacitor will have a large reactance X_C and current I will be small

blocks.prompt: 43 Find the reactance of a 2 μF capacitor at 1 kHz.

book_ref.quote: The unit of capacitive reactance X_C is ohm and is given as:

blocks.prompt: 44 Differentiate between the behaviour of an inductor and a capacitor in AC circuits.
blocks.explanation: In an inductor the current lags the voltage by 90°; in a capacitor it leads by 90°.

book_ref.quote: Unlike a resistor, a capacitor behaves differently in AC and DC circuits.

rows: Current lags behind the voltage by 90°.
Current leads the voltage by 90°.
X_L = 2πfL, increases with frequency.
X_C = 1/(2πfC), decreases with frequency.
Allows DC (X_L = 0 at f = 0).
Blocks DC (X_C = ∞ at f = 0).
Stores energy in a magnetic field.
Stores energy in an electric field.

blocks.prompt: 45 Who is called the father of alternating currents and why?
blocks.explanation: Nikola Tesla (born 1856, emigrated to the U.S.A. in 1884). He pioneered the generation, transmission and use of alternating current, which can be transmitted over much greater distances than direct current.

book_ref.quote: Nikola Tesla was born in 1856 in Austria-Hungary

blocks.prompt: 46 Define impedance and give its SI unit.
blocks.explanation: Impedance Z is the combined effect of resistance and reactances in an AC circuit. It is the ratio of the rms voltage to the rms current: Z = Vᵣₘₛ/Iᵣₘₛ. Its SI unit is ohm.

book_ref.quote: The combined effect of resistance and reactances in such circuits is known as impedance.

blocks.prompt: 47 Differentiate between resistance and reactance.
blocks.explanation: Resistance is opposition due to resistors; reactance is opposition due to capacitors and inductors.

book_ref.quote: Reactance is the opposition to current flow due to capacitors

rows: Opposition to current due to resistors.
Opposition to current due to inductors (X_L) and capacitors (X_C).
Same for DC and AC; V and I in phase.
Depends on frequency (X_L = 2πfL, X_C = 1/2πfC); V and I differ by 90°.
Energy is dissipated as heat.
No average power is dissipated; energy is stored and returned.

blocks.prompt: 48 A circuit draws an rms current of 2.2 A from a 110 V rms supply. Find its impedance.
blocks.explanation: Z = Vᵣₘₛ/Iᵣₘₛ = 110 V/2.2 A = 50 Ω.

book_ref.quote: It is the ratio of the rms value of the voltage to the rms value of the current.

blocks.prompt: 49 What is an impedance diagram? Draw its idea for an RC-series circuit in words.
blocks.explanation: In an impedance diagram, R is drawn as a horizontal line along the current (the reference); X_C = 1/ωC is drawn lagging the R line by 90°. Their vector sum is the impedance Z = √(R² + X_C²), and the angle of Z with the R line is the phase angle θ.

book_ref.quote: The impedance Z of the circuit is obtained by the vector summation of resistance and reactance.

blocks.prompt: 50 Why is the power in an RC-series circuit consumed only by the resistor?
blocks.explanation: The capacitor only stores energy in its electric field and returns it; it does not dissipate it. Hence the power is consumed by the resistor: P = I²R = VI cos θ.

book_ref.quote: The power consumed in RC-series circuit is primarily due to the resistor

blocks.prompt: 51 An 80 Ω resistor is in series with a capacitor of reactance 60 Ω. Find the impedance and the phase angle.
blocks.explanation: Z = √(R² + X_C²) = √(80² + 60²) = 100 Ω. θ = tan⁻¹(X_C/R) = tan⁻¹(60/80) = 36.9°, the current leading the voltage.

book_ref.quote: Equation 17.21 suggests that we can find the impedance of a series AC circuit by vector addition.

blocks.prompt: 52 Write the phase relations of V_R and V_L with the current in an RL-series circuit and the resulting rms voltage.
blocks.explanation: V_R = IᵣₘₛR is in phase with the current; V_L = IᵣₘₛX_L leads the current by 90°. Their vector sum is Vᵣₘₛ = √(V_R² + V_L²) = Iᵣₘₛ√(R² + ω²L²).

book_ref.quote: Voltage V across L is ahead of current I through L by 90°

blocks.prompt: 53 A 12 Ω resistor is in series with a coil of reactance 5 Ω. Find the impedance and phase angle.
blocks.explanation: Z = √(R² + X_L²) = √(12² + 5²) = 13 Ω. θ = tan⁻¹(X_L/R) = tan⁻¹(5/12) = 22.6°, the voltage leading the current.

book_ref.quote: Consider an AC circuit containing a resistor R and inductor L connected in series

blocks.prompt: 54 How does an electric eel produce powerful shocks?
blocks.explanation: Through its 3 main organs, making up about 80% of its body length, made of specialised cells called electrocytes (the book prints 'electrolytes', which are conducting solutions).

book_ref.quote: through specialized cells called electrolytes

blocks.prompt: 55 What is power factor? What is its value for a pure resistor?
blocks.explanation: In P = VI cos θ, the factor cos θ, where θ is the phase angle between voltage and current, is the power factor. For a pure resistor θ = 0, so the power factor is 1.

book_ref.quote: The factor cos θ is known as power factor.

blocks.prompt: 56 A DC solar panel gives 600 W to an inverter of efficiency 85%. How much AC power is received?
blocks.explanation: P_ac = (inverter efficiency) × P_dc = 0.85 × 600 W = 510 W.

book_ref.quote: So, we can find AC power from DC power by using the following conversion as:

blocks.prompt: 57 About how much electricity does a 1.5 ton air conditioner use in one hour?
blocks.explanation: About 1.2 to 1.5 units (kWh) per hour.

book_ref.quote: The electricity consumption of a 1.5 ton A.C is approximately

blocks.prompt: 58 How does an RLC-series circuit behave at very high and at very low frequencies?
blocks.explanation: At high frequency X_L = ωL ≫ X_C, so the inductive reactance dominates and the circuit behaves as an RL-series circuit. At low frequency X_C = 1/ωC ≫ X_L, so it behaves as an RC-series circuit.

book_ref.quote: When frequency is high, then X_L = ωL is much greater than X_C = 1/ω C

blocks.prompt: 59 What is resonance in an RLC-series circuit? Write the resonance frequency.
blocks.explanation: Resonance is the condition at the frequency where X_L = X_C; the equal and opposite reactances cancel and the circuit behaves as a pure resistive circuit. From ωᵣL = 1/ωᵣC, fᵣ = 1/(2π√LC).

book_ref.quote: This condition is called resonance.

blocks.prompt: 60 Find the resonance frequency of an RLC-series circuit with L = 25 mH and C = 0.4 μF.

book_ref.quote: In between these frequencies, there will be a frequency ωᵣ at which X_L = X_C.

blocks.prompt: 61 Why is the current maximum at resonance in an RLC-series circuit?
blocks.explanation: At resonance X_L = X_C, so Z = √(R² + 0) = R, the minimum possible impedance. With minimum impedance the current I = V/Z reaches its maximum value, in phase with the voltage.

book_ref.quote: At resonance, the current in the circuit reaches its maximum value

blocks.prompt: 62 How is the motion of a car wheel on its spring analogous to an RLC-series circuit?
blocks.explanation: The forced, damped motion of the wheel is like the AC in an RLC circuit: the shock absorber damps the motion and dissipates energy like the resistance, while the mass and spring determine the resonant frequency.

book_ref.quote: The forced but damped motion of the wheel on the car spring is analogous

blocks.prompt: 63 What is voltage amplification in an RLC-series circuit?
blocks.explanation: At resonance, the voltage across the inductor and across the capacitor can be much higher than the applied voltage because of the large circulating current. This is voltage amplification.

book_ref.quote: the voltage across the inductor and capacitor can be significantly higher than the applied voltage

blocks.prompt: 64 Differentiate between true power and apparent power.
blocks.explanation: True power is VI cos θ (watt); apparent power is VI (volt-ampere).

book_ref.quote: However, the power dissipation in impedance is called apparent power

rows: P = VᵣₘₛIᵣₘₛ cos θ (Eq. 17.27).
S = VᵣₘₛIᵣₘₛ.
Power actually dissipated (in the resistance).
Product of rms voltage and rms current, without the power factor.
Measured in watts.
Measured in volt-amperes.
Maximum when θ = 0.
Equals true power only when θ = 0.

blocks.prompt: 65 In an RLC-series circuit, V_L = 25 V, V_C = 10 V and V_R = 20 V. Find the source voltage and the phase angle.

book_ref.quote: In a LCR-circuit, an inductor having inductive voltage 20 V

blocks.prompt: 66 Differentiate between RLC-series and RLC-parallel circuits at resonance.
blocks.explanation: Series: impedance minimum and current maximum; parallel: impedance maximum and current minimum.

book_ref.quote: A RLC-parallel circuit is one where the resistor, inductor and capacitor are connected in parallel

rows: Same current through R, L and C.
Same voltage across R, L and C.
Impedance is minimum (Z = R).
Impedance is maximum.
Current is maximum.
Source current is minimum.
Gives voltage amplification across L and C.
Gives current magnification in the L and C branches.

blocks.prompt: 67 What is admittance? Why is it useful for parallel circuits?
blocks.explanation: Admittance Y is the reciprocal of impedance (Y = 1/Z). It is used to analyse parallel circuits because the total admittance of a parallel RLC circuit is simply the sum of the admittances of the individual components.

book_ref.quote: The total admittance of a parallel RLC-circuit is the sum of the admittances

blocks.prompt: 68 What is meant by current magnification in an RLC-parallel circuit?
blocks.explanation: At resonance the source current is minimum, but the branch currents I_L and I_C may each be much larger than the resonance current Iᵣ. This magnification of current in the branches is current magnification.

book_ref.quote: At resonance, the branch currents IL and IC may each be larger than the resonance current Iᵣ.

blocks.prompt: 69 How is an RLC-parallel circuit used in an induction cooktop?
blocks.explanation: Its resonant behaviour matches the desired heating frequency: the circuit generates a high frequency current in the coil, which induces currents in the metal cookware, and these currents heat the cookware.

book_ref.quote: the RLC-parallel circuit generates a high frequency current in the coil

blocks.prompt: 70 What does the quality factor of a resonant circuit indicate? How does it depend on R for a parallel RLC circuit?
blocks.explanation: The quality factor Q measures the sharpness of the resonance peak, i.e. how much energy is stored compared with the energy dissipated. For a parallel RLC circuit Q = R√(C/L), so Q is directly proportional to R.

book_ref.quote: indicates how much energy is stored in the circuit compared to the energy dissipated

blocks.prompt: 71 What is rectification? Why is it needed in computers and smartphones?
blocks.explanation: Rectification is the process of converting alternating current into direct current. Computers and smartphones need a stable DC power source, while most household and commercial power is AC, so it must be rectified.

book_ref.quote: Rectification is the process of converting alternating current into direct current.

blocks.prompt: 72 Which property of a diode makes it suitable for rectification?
blocks.explanation: A diode allows a large current when forward biased, but the current through a reverse-biased diode is practically zero. Since it lets current flow in one direction only, it converts AC into unidirectional current (DC).

book_ref.quote: It is due to this important property of the diode that it can be used for rectification

blocks.prompt: 73 Why are mobile phone batteries charged with DC?
blocks.explanation: Batteries store DC, since DC is easier to store than AC, and DC is also safer. The grid gives only AC, so a rectifier converts it to DC before charging phones, laptops and flashlights.

book_ref.quote: DC is also safer compared to AC.

blocks.prompt: 74 Explain the working of a half-wave rectifier during the two halves of the input cycle.
blocks.explanation: During 0 → T/2 the diode is forward biased, offers very low resistance and current flows through R_L. During T/2 → T it is reverse biased, offers very high resistance and practically no current flows. So the output is current in one direction, in pulses.

book_ref.quote: the diode D is forward bias, so it offers a very low resistance and current flows through R_L

blocks.prompt: 75 Differentiate between half-wave and full-wave rectification.
blocks.explanation: Half-wave uses one half-cycle; full-wave uses both half-cycles.

book_ref.quote: Rectification during which both halves of alternating input voltage are converted

rows: Passes one half-cycle and blocks the other.
Both halves of the input are converted into unidirectional current.
One diode in series with the load R_L.
Bridge of four diodes, two conducting in each half-cycle.
No output during the blocked half-cycle.
Output in both half-cycles, in the same direction through the load.

blocks.prompt: 76 Which diodes of a bridge rectifier conduct during each half-cycle, and why is the load current in the same direction?
blocks.explanation: During the positive half-cycle (A positive) D₁ and D₂ conduct in series while D₃ and D₄ are reverse biased; during the negative half-cycle (B positive) D₃ and D₄ conduct and D₁, D₂ are off. In both cases the current passes through the load in the same direction.

book_ref.quote: Now the diodes D₃ and D₄ conduct in series

blocks.prompt: 77 Write any four uses of the PN junction diode.
blocks.explanation: Rectification, signal clipping, voltage regulation, clamping voltage (also signal detection, photovoltaic cells and switching light emission).

book_ref.quote: Uses of the PN junction diode

blocks.prompt: 78 How does a smoothing capacitor reduce the ripple in a rectifier output?
blocks.explanation: The capacitor is connected in parallel with the load. It charges when the rectified voltage increases and discharges into the load when the voltage decreases, filling the gaps, so the pulsating output becomes smoother DC with a higher average level.

book_ref.quote: It charges when the rectified voltage increases and discharges when the voltage decreases

blocks.prompt: 79 A bridge rectifier on a 50 Hz supply gives a load current of 0.1 A with a 500 μF smoothing capacitor. Find the ripple voltage and ripple frequency.

blocks.prompt: 85 Where is energy stored in an inductor? Why can it never be negative?
blocks.explanation: Energy is stored in the magnetic field of the inductor: U_m = ½LI². Since it is proportional to the square of the current, it can never be negative; the inductor stores energy while absorbing power and returns it while delivering power.

blocks.prompt: 88 Define mutual induction and describe briefly how it is shown with two coils.
blocks.explanation: Mutual induction: a changing current in one coil induces an emf in another coil. The primary (with battery, switch and rheostat) is placed near the secondary (with galvanometer); changing the primary current changes the flux linking the secondary and the galvanometer deflects.

book_ref.quote: This causes an induced emf in the secondary.

blocks.prompt: 89 Define mutual inductance and its unit henry.
blocks.explanation: Mutual inductance M is the ratio of the emf induced in the secondary to the time rate of change of current in the primary: M = εₛ/(ΔIₚ/Δt). Its unit is V s A⁻¹ = henry: one henry when a change of 1 A s⁻¹ in the primary induces 1 V in the secondary.

blocks.prompt: 91 An emf of 5 V is induced in a secondary coil when the primary current changes at 50 A s⁻¹. Find the mutual inductance.
blocks.explanation: M = εₛ/(ΔIₚ/Δt) = 5 V/50 A s⁻¹ = 0.1 H.

blocks.prompt: 92 Differentiate between self-induction and mutual induction.
blocks.explanation: Self-induction acts within one coil; mutual induction acts between two coils.
